title: Month-end bank reconciliation — Meridian Building Group operating account
scenario: You are the controller closing March 2026 for Meridian Building Group. The general ledger cash balance (account 1000, operating) is $653,775. The Riverton Community Bank statement shows an ending balance of $699,000. Reconcile book to bank, identify reconciling items, and record the journal entries for the BOOK-side adjustments only (bank-side items — deposits in transit and outstanding checks — are timing differences that need no entry; they clear themselves). The reconciled (true) cash balance must agree to the adjusted Q1 cash reported on the trial balance.

exhibits.title: Starting balances
exhibits.body: GL cash per books (acct 1000): $653,775. Bank statement ending balance: $699,000.

exhibits.title: Bank-side reconciling items (timing — no journal entry)

rows.note: Customer ACH/checks deposited 3/31, not yet on bank statement.
Vendor checks written/mailed, not yet cleared the bank.
Customer check from Cedar Ridge Holdings bounced; reinstate the receivable.
Monthly account analysis and wire fees.
Interest credited on the operating sweep.
Check to Apex Steel written for $5,400 but recorded in the GL as $4,500; cash is overstated by $900.

tasks.prompt: Compute the adjusted bank balance: bank statement balance + deposits in transit − outstanding checks.
Compute the adjusted book balance: GL cash − NSF − bank fees + interest − bookkeeping error.
Confirm the reconciled cash balance (both sides must agree) and that it equals the trial-balance cash.
tasks.explanation: Adjusted bank 642,300 = adjusted book 642,300 = TB account 1000 cash 642,300. Reconciled.

tasks.prompt: Record the BOOK-side adjusting journal entries (no entries for deposits in transit or outstanding checks). Reinstate the NSF as a receivable, expense the bank fees, record interest income, and correct the check #4471 understatement.

checks.netCashAdjustment: Cash entries: −12,000 − 425 + 1,850 − 900 = −11,475, which moves GL cash from 653,775 to 642,300.
checks.balanced: Each compound entry balances Dr = Cr.

tasks.explanation: NSF: Dr AR 12,000 / Cr Cash 12,000 (the customer still owes; cash never truly arrived). Fees: Dr G&A 425 / Cr Cash 425. Interest: Dr Cash 1,850 / Cr Interest income 1,850. Check #4471 error: the check was $5,400 but booked at $4,500, so cash and AP are both overstated by $900 — Dr AP 900 / Cr Cash 900 corrects both. Net cash change −11,475 ties GL cash 653,775 down to the reconciled 642,300.

tasks.prompt: Write a 3-4 sentence note for the month-end close file explaining why deposits in transit and outstanding checks get NO journal entry, while NSF, fees, interest, and the recording error DO.
tasks.explanation: Bank-side items (deposits in transit, outstanding checks) are timing differences the bank will record on its own when the items clear — the books are already correct, so no entry. Book-side items (NSF, fees, interest, the $900 recording error) are transactions or errors the general ledger has not yet captured, so they require journal entries to state cash correctly.

gradingRules.je: debits = credits per entry; only book-side items posted; net cash effect = −11,475
gradingRules.writeup: keyword + correctness on the timing vs. book-error distinction

conversationSim.prompt: The outside CPA asks: 'Your GL cash was $653,775 but the reconciled balance is $642,300 — a $11,475 swing. Walk me through it and tell me which pieces actually hit the income statement.' Draft the answer.
conversationSim.modelAnswer: The $11,475 reduction is four book-side items the GL hadn't captured before close. The NSF check ($12,000) reduced cash but moved back to accounts receivable, so it's a balance-sheet reclass, not an expense — Cedar Ridge still owes us. Bank fees ($425) hit G&A expense and interest income ($1,850) is other income, so the net P&L effect is only $1,425 of additional pretax income. The $900 was a recording error — check #4471 was written for $5,400 but booked at $4,500 — so correcting it reduces both cash and accounts payable with no P&L impact. After these, GL cash agrees to the bank at $642,300.
